gaps.sentence: I will always remember the summer ___ we cycled along the Danube.
gaps.explanation: 'When' relates to a time expression like 'the summer'.
'What happened next' means 'the thing that happened'; 'that' cannot introduce the clause here because the sentence needs a subject inside it.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ the flight was diverted has never been made public.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' — 'why' is the relative for reasons.

gaps.sentence: The manager, for ___ the team played so hard, thanked everyone.
gaps.hint: played for the manager — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: The preposition 'for' demands the object form 'whom' for a person.

gaps.sentence: We must decide ___ to do next.
gaps.explanation: 'What to do' is the standard pattern meaning 'the thing that we should do'.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: The cafe ___ we first met has closed down.
gaps.hint: location: we met in the cafe
gaps.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' for places; 'which' would need a preposition ('in which').

gaps.sentence: They said nothing at all, ___ I found rather strange.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' here means 'and this'; it refers to the whole situation and follows a comma.
